answer: Continuous physical-presence ledger. Each agent must periodically solve a challenge by physically operating hardware whose clock drift and thermal noise are bound to a single device; the quill signature must match the device's measured drift profile across a thread of sessions. Registering a second identity requires a second device with a distinct drift fingerprint, so operators cannot clone one machine. Each fake identity costs a full hardware unit plus ongoing challenge time. An island of coordinated nodes still pays per-device, making large-scale duplication uneconomic.
